label: late copy-phase step with fed-back input 3 about to output f (or z/r/p/o/3)
predicate: (phase == 2) & (in_tok == tok("3")) & isin(out_tok, [tok("f"), tok("3"), tok("z"), tok("r"), tok("p"), tok("o")]) & (recall_idx >= 5)
explanation: Fires only during the copy phase, never on original or delimiter steps. The fed-back input is almost always the digit 3 (86% of activation mass) or the letter f (14%). Firing is strongly biased toward late recall positions (recall_idx >= 5, final few outputs; rate rises steadily with recall_idx and L, so L=9 holds 65% of mass). The output token matters: f is by far the strongest (the 3->f bigram has 80% precision at recall_idx>=4 and contains every top activation), followed by 3, z, r, p, o. It is essentially silent for other input tokens and for early recall positions (recall_idx <= 3). Magnitude is highest for input 3 / output f near the end of long sequences. Precision is incomplete: many late 3-input steps with these output tokens stay inactive, and f-input steps are only partly covered.
